text: react-window is a component library that helps render large lists of data quickly and without the performance problems that often go along with rendering a lot of data. It's used in a lot of places, from React DevTools to the Replay browser. If you've never used a library like this before, you may want to read the how it works section first. Installation Begin by installing the library from NPM: npm install react-window TypeScript definitions are included within the published dist folder. Support Here are some ways to support this project: Become a GitHub sponsor Buy me a coffee

headings.title: cellComponent
headings.text:
cellComponent: (props: { ariaAttributes: { "aria-colindex": number; role: "gridcell"; }; columnIndex: number; rowIndex: number; style: CSSProperties; } & CellProps) => ReactNode | null React component responsible for rendering a cell.
 This component will receive columnIndex, rowIndex, and style props by default.
Additionally it will receive prop values passed to cellProps.
 The prop types for this component are exported as CellComponentProps

headings.title: cellProps
headings.text:
cellProps: CellProps Additional props to be passed to the cell-rendering component.
Grid will automatically re-render cells when values in this object change.
 This object must not contain ariaAttributes, columnIndex, rowIndex, or style props.

headings.title: columnCount
headings.text: columnCount: number Number of columns to be rendered in the grid.

headings.title: columnWidth
headings.text:
columnWidth: string | number | ((index: number, cellProps: CellProps) => number) Column width; the following formats are supported:

number of pixels (number)
percentage of the grid's current width (string)
function that returns the column width (in pixels) given an index and cellProps 

 Percentage widths can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultWidth (or a pixel width via the style prop) is specified.

headings.title: rowCount
headings.text: rowCount: number Number of rows to be rendered in the grid.

headings.title: rowHeight
headings.text:
rowHeight: string | number | ((index: number, cellProps: CellProps) => number) Row height; the following formats are supported:

number of pixels (number)
percentage of the grid's current height (string)
function that returns the row height (in pixels) given an index and cellProps 

 Percentage heights can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) is specified.

headings.title: children
headings.text:
children?: ReactNode Additional content to be rendered within the grid (above cells).
This property can be used to render things like overlays or tooltips.

headings.title: className
headings.text: className?: string CSS class name.

headings.title: columnKey
headings.text:
columnKey?: (args: { columnIndex: number; data: CellProps; rowIndex: number; }) => Key Grids use the column index as a key by default.
This prop can be used along with the rowKey prop to provide a custom key value.
 Custom keys can ensure better UX for sortable or filterable grids,
particularly if your cell components are stateful.
Refer to the React documentation for more info.
 This prop cannot be auto-memoized because it is called during render.
It is important to always useCallback for this prop; do not use an inline function.

headings.title: defaultHeight
headings.text:
defaultHeight?: number = 0 Default height of grid (in pixels) for initial render, before its actual height has been measured.
 Grids can't be measured during server rendering, so this value determines how many rows are server rendered.
It's recommended to set this to the expected height of the grid (or to specify a pixel height via the style prop).

headings.title: defaultScrollLeft
headings.text:
defaultScrollLeft?: number = 0 Initial horizontal scroll offset (in pixels) of the grid.
This value is only applied once, when the grid first mounts with at least one column.
 Server-rendered HTML can't be pre-scrolled, so server rendering always starts at the first column;
the default scroll offset is applied once the grid hydrates.
 If the grid can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none,
or uses percentage column widths before its width has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried.
Specify a defaultWidth (or a pixel width via the style prop) when using percentage column widths.

headings.title: defaultScrollTop
headings.text:
defaultScrollTop?: number = 0 Initial vertical scroll offset (in pixels) of the grid.
This value is only applied once, when the grid first mounts with at least one row.
 Server-rendered HTML can't be pre-scrolled, so server rendering always starts at the first row;
the default scroll offset is applied once the grid hydrates.
 If the grid can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none,
or uses percentage row heights before its height has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried.
Specify a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) when using percentage row heights.

headings.title: defaultWidth
headings.text:
defaultWidth?: number = 0 Default width of grid (in pixels) for initial render, before its actual width has been measured.
 Grids can't be measured during server rendering, so this value determines how many columns are server rendered.
It's recommended to set this to the expected width of the grid (or to specify a pixel width via the style prop).

headings.title: dir
headings.text:
dir?: string Indicates the directionality of grid cells.
 The directionality of an ancestor element can't be detected during server rendering;
specify this prop explicitly for server-rendered right-to-left grids.
 See HTML dir global attribute for more information.

headings.title: gridRef
headings.text:
gridRef?: Ref<{ readonly element: HTMLDivElement | null; scrollToCell(config: { behavior?: "auto" | "instant" | "smooth"; columnAlign?: "auto" | "center" | "end" | "smart" | "start"; columnIndex: number; rowAlign?: "auto" | ... 3 more ... | "start"; rowIndex: number; }): void; scrollToColumn(config: { ...; }): void; scrollToR... Imperative Grid API.
 The useGridRef and useGridCallbackRef hooks are exported for convenience in TypeScript projects.

headings.title: onCellsRendered
headings.text: onCellsRendered?: (visibleCells: { columnStartIndex: number; columnStopIndex: number; rowStartIndex: number; rowStopIndex: number; }, allCells: { columnStartIndex: number; columnStopIndex: number; rowStartIndex: number; rowStopIndex: number; }) => void Callback notified when the range of rendered cells changes.

headings.title: onResize
headings.text:
onResize?: (size: { height: number; width: number; }, prevSize: { height: number; width: number; }) => void Callback notified when the Grid's outermost HTMLElement resizes.
This may be used to (re)scroll a cell into view.

headings.title: overscanCount
headings.text:
overscanCount?: number = 3 How many additional rows/columns to render outside of the visible area.
This can reduce visual flickering near the edges of a grid when scrolling.

headings.title: rowKey
headings.text:
rowKey?: (args: { data: CellProps; rowIndex: number; }) => Key Grids use the row index as a key by default.
This prop can be used along with the columnKey prop to provide a custom key value.
 Custom keys can ensure better UX for sortable or filterable grids,
particularly if your cell components are stateful.
Refer to the React documentation for more info.
 This prop cannot be auto-memoized because it is called during render.
It is important to always useCallback for this prop; do not use an inline function.

headings.title: scrollElement
headings.text:
scrollElement?: HTMLElement | "window" | null Element that scrolls the grid, for grids that scroll along with other content (e.g. the page):

"window" to scroll with the page
an ancestor element that scrolls (e.g. stored with a useState ref callback); null until it has mounted

 The grid renders at its full height and only renders the rows (and columns) visible within the scroll element's viewport.
Its position within the scroll element is measured whenever it renders, scrolls, or resizes,
and whenever content before it is resized, inserted, or removed (e.g. an image loading above the grid).

columns scroll with the scroll element too if the grid is as wide as its content (e.g. style={{ width: "max-content" }});
otherwise the grid fills the width of its parent and its columns scroll within it
 scrollToCell, scrollToColumn and scrollToRow scroll whichever element scrolls each axis
 defaultHeight and defaultWidth are used as the viewport size until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering)
percentage row heights and column widths are relative to the scroll element's viewport
 defaultScrollLeft and defaultScrollTop are ignored

 While the scroll element is null, the grid renders the first rows (as it does during server rendering).
 The grid's onScroll handler is only called when the grid scrolls its own columns;
listen to the scroll element's "scroll" events instead (or use the useIsScrolling hook).

headings.title: style
headings.text:
style?: CSSProperties Optional CSS properties.
The grid of cells will fill the height and width defined by this style.

headings.title: tagName
headings.text:
tagName?: keyof IntrinsicElements = "div" as TagName Can be used to override the root HTML element rendered by the Grid component.
The default value is "div", meaning that Grid renders an HTMLDivElement as its root.
 In most use cases the default ARIA roles are sufficient and this prop is not needed.

text: The useIsScrolling hook tracks whether a list is scrolling. Rows can use this value to render simplified content while scrolling, as shown below. Scrolling ends when the browser fires a scrollend event. Browsers that don't support that event wait until no scroll events have been received for a short delay (150ms by default; configurable with the delay option).

headings.title: rowComponent
headings.text:
rowComponent: (props: { ariaAttributes: { "aria-posinset": number; "aria-setsize": number; role: "listitem"; }; index: number; style: CSSProperties; } & RowProps) => ReactNode | null React component responsible for rendering a row.
 This component will receive an index and style prop by default.
Additionally it will receive prop values passed to rowProps.
 The prop types for this component are exported as RowComponentProps

headings.title: rowCount
headings.text: rowCount: number Number of items to be rendered in the list.

headings.title: rowHeight
headings.text:
rowHeight: string | number | DynamicRowHeight | ((index: number, cellProps: RowProps) => number) Row height; the following formats are supported:

number of pixels (number)
percentage of the list's current height (string)
function that returns the row height (in pixels) given an index and rowProps 
dynamic row height cache returned by the useDynamicRowHeight hook

 Percentage heights can't be resolved during server rendering unless a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) is specified.
 Dynamic row heights are not as efficient as predetermined sizes.
It's recommended to provide your own height values if they can be determined ahead of time.

 If the list can't be scrolled that far when the offset is applied (e.g. it is hidden with display: none,
or uses percentage row heights before its height has been measured), the offset is clamped or ignored and not retried.
Specify a defaultHeight (or a pixel height via the style prop) when using percentage row heights.

text: This library requires React version 18 or newer. It also uses the ResizeObserver (or a polyfill) to calculate the available space for List and Grid components. ResizeObserver usage can be avoided if explicit pixel dimensions are specified using the style prop. (Percentage or EM/REM based dimensions do not count.)
title: Requirements

Right to left content
headings.text: Right to left content Grids inherit their direction from ancestor elements, but this can't be detected on the server. Specify the dir prop explicitly for server-rendered right-to-left grids.

headings.title: Scrollbar size
headings.text: Scrollbar size getScrollbarSize returns 0 on the server. To avoid hydration mismatches, read it after the component has mounted (e.g. within an effect) instead of during render. Click below for more guidance about server rendering. Server rendering with React Server Components Server rendering with dynamic row heights Server rendering with an initial scroll position

text: List and Grid can be rendered on the server (including static site generation and React Server Components). Server-rendered rows are visible before JavaScript has loaded, and they hydrate without mismatches.

text: GitHub is the easiest place to look for help, but it's probably not the fastest. This project is maintained by a single developer so there is limited bandwidth for answering questions. I recommend asking questions on Stack Overflow or Reddit to start with. Both sites have active communities who often respond quickly. If you don't find an answer there you can try opening a GitHub issue- but please take a moment first to see if your question has has already been answered before opening a new one.
